meta.title: Sirrak — private, offline Arabic AI assistant for Android
meta.description: Sirrak runs a real Arabic-English language model on your Android phone: offline chat, dictation, document answers and model control. No account, no cloud, no telemetry. Apache-2.0.

hero.headline:
Your own assistant.
It never leaves your phone.
hero.lead: Sirrak runs a real language model, Arabic dictation and document search on your Android phone. No account, no cloud, no telemetry — every network request is one you start: a model download, a Hugging Face search, or a capped file-header check.
meta: libre flavour · SHA-256 in release notes

screenshot.alt: Sirrak home screen in Arabic with a model ready and the composer at the bottom

steps.title: The first ten minutes
steps.lead: Four numbered moves take you from a fresh install to an assistant that answers without a network. Every screenshot below is the shipping build on a real emulator, not a mockup.

items.title: Bring a model — or start with the demo
items.body: Onboarding recommends a model that fits your phone and downloads it with resume and a checksum. No model is bundled: every catalogue entry shows its licence before you download it.

screenshot.alt: Model manager with a recommended model and storage details

items.callout: Recommended for your device, with licence shown up front

items.title: Ask in Arabic and watch the answer stream
items.body: Chat runs on-device through llama.cpp. Stop mid-answer, regenerate, or start a clean conversation; the transcript survives process death and can be exported as Markdown.

screenshot.alt: Arabic chat answer streaming with copy and regenerate actions

items.callout: Tokens per second are measured, not estimated

items.title: Dictate instead of typing
items.body: On-device Whisper transcribes Arabic or English. The recording strip keeps a live timer while it listens; the transcript is appended to the composer — never sent on its own — and the audio never leaves the phone.

screenshot.alt: Dictation recording strip with its timer and stop/cancel controls above the composer

items.callout: The compose bridge: speech lands as text you can edit

items.title: Own the network
items.body: Turn on offline-only and the app cannot open a socket, including model downloads. The network log lists the calls that actually happened on this device, bounded to 50 entries and never uploaded.

screenshot.alt: Privacy settings with the offline-only switch and network log

items.callout: No background calls: every network request is one you start

inventory.title: What is in the box
inventory.lead: Everything below ships in the same Apache-2.0 app. Nothing needs an account, and nothing phones home.

items.title: Local chat
items.body: Streaming answers from a GGUF model, multiple conversations with search and rename, Markdown rendering, per-conversation prompts and stop sequences.

items.title: Arabic & English dictation
items.body: sherpa-onnx Whisper on the device, a recording strip with a live timer, and a transcript that waits in the composer until you send it.

items.title: Answers from your documents
items.body: Import PDF, DOCX, EPUB, Markdown or text, index locally, and ask with citations you can open — retrieval is embeddings plus Arabic BM25.

items.title: Model control
items.body: A curated catalogue with device-aware recommendations (including a compact 2 GB tier), resumable checksum-verified downloads, a storage manager and Hugging Face import.

items.title: Engine control
items.body: Temperature, top-p, top-k, repeat penalty, context size, chat templates and prompts — data layers whose effective values are provable in one log line.

items.title: Privacy surfaces
items.body: Offline-only enforcement, a per-call network audit, local AI-output reports with an explicit share step, and honest status instead of dead links.

privacy.title: Privacy you can check, not just read
privacy.lead: A privacy promise is worth what its evidence is worth. Sirrak declares its endpoints in configuration, audits the calls that actually happen, and gives you a switch that stops the app at the socket.

points.title: No telemetry, ever
points.body: No analytics, no crash service, no ads, no account. There is no server to receive your conversations, documents or reports.

points.title: A network log on the device
points.body: Every call that actually happened appears in a bounded local log — written for you, never uploaded, cleared with the app's data.

points.title: Offline-only is enforced first
points.body: The switch is checked before a socket opens and cancels a running download instead of queuing it.

points.title: Storage stays app-private
points.body: Chats, documents, embeddings, models and settings live in app-private storage; sharing only happens through the Android chooser you invoke.

download.title: Download and verify
download.lead: The published libre APK is signed with the project certificate and built from the 1.0.0-rc2 tag. The 1.1.0 features described on this page are not in that build yet: its signed release is still pending. You can verify the published build before installing.

steps.title: Get the signed APK
steps.body: Open the latest release on GitHub and download the signed 1.0.0-rc2 libre APK (~139 MiB, universal arm64-v8a + x86_64).

steps.title: Verify the certificate
steps.body: Run apksigner verify --print-certs and compare SHA-256 with the fingerprint below. SHA-256 checksums are in the release notes.

steps.title: Install, pick a model, go offline
steps.body: Android 9+ is required. Choose a model in onboarding or start with the demo engine, then switch offline-only when you are ready.

items.a: Yes. After you import or download a model, the chat, dictation, document search and settings run without a network. Offline-only mode blocks every request and cancels a running download.

items.q: Is it free? What is the catch?
items.a: Sirrak is free software under Apache-2.0, with no accounts, ads or telemetry. Models are not bundled and may carry their own licences; gated models need your own Hugging Face token, kept in memory only.
Android 9 (API 28) or newer on arm64. The x86_64 build is for emulators and development. The app warns before a download that would leave too little storage.

items.q: Where do the models come from?
items.a: A curated catalogue with recommendations (Qwen2.5, LFM2.5 350M for 2 GB phones and other GGUF models), a local GGUF import, or a Hugging Face repository import. Every model's licence is shown before download; nothing is bundled.
The native llama.cpp and sherpa-onnx runtimes are compiled into the app, so it works without extra downloads. Model weights are separate and can be several hundred MiB.

items.q: How do I know the claims are true?
items.a: The source, build records, tests, screenshots and release signatures are public in this repository. The website itself is generated from committed data and has no third-party scripts.
